what: The score is Δ − 2d(depot, customer) − 0.5R·q/rem, where Δ is the fixed-position insertion increase, R is the current route's maximum depot radius, and q/rem is the candidate's bounded fraction of remaining capacity. It runs in O(len(route)) time, scans no completed routes or full instance, and returns a finite float.
why: Subtracting the candidate's singleton-route cost turns raw cheapest insertion into a generalized savings criterion: it rewards customers whose insertion avoids substantial depot travel and tends to preserve geographically coherent, outward routes rather than systematically preferring near-depot customers. The modest capacity term favors useful packing, especially late in a route, without overwhelming geometric savings. This is a construction heuristic rather than a remaining-cost estimate; it cannot alter the prescribed insertion position, and its packing bias may occasionally reject a geometrically preferable small-demand customer. The formula has not been empirically validated on the supplied or held-out instances.
